questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which one of the following is not a criterion for classification of fungi?
questions.explanation: The morphology of the mycelium, mode of spore formation and fruiting bodies form the basis for classification of the kingdom fungi into various classes. All fungi derive their nutrition through the heterotrophic mode, which is not a distinguishing criterion among them.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Rhizopus, (B) Ustilago, (C) Puccinia, (D) Agaricus
List-II: (I) Mushroom, (II) Smut fungus, (III) Bread mould, (IV) Rust fungus
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Agaricus (mushroom), Ustilago (smut) and Puccinia (rust fungus) are common Basidiomycetes. Rhizopus (bread mould) belongs to Phycomycetes. So A-(III), B-(II), C-(IV), D-(I).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Identify the part of the seed from the given figure which is destined to form root when the seed germinates. The figure is a longitudinal section of a monocot (grass-type) seed showing the pericarp and endosperm on the outside, and within the embryo region four labeled parts from top to bottom: A (coleoptile, the sheath around the plumule), B (plumule, the embryonic shoot), C (radicle, the embryonic root, shown centrally), and D (coleorhiza, the sheath around the radicle).
questions.explanation: The primary root, or radicle, is the first organ to appear when a seed germinates. Per the labeled figure (Pericarp, Endosperm, Scutellum, Coleoptile=A, Plumule=B, Radicle=C, Coleorhiza=D), the radicle is part C.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Identify the type of flowers based on the position of calyx, corolla and androecium with respect to the ovary from the given figures (A) and (B): two floral longitudinal-section diagrams, each showing petals and stamens arranged around a central gynoecium at approximately the same level on the rim of a cup-shaped thalamus (both figures show the same general perigynous arrangement, differing slightly in petal shading/shape).
questions.explanation: Both given figures (A) and (B) show perigynous flowers. In a perigynous flower, the gynoecium is situated in the centre and the other floral parts are located on the rim of the thalamus at almost the same level; the ovary is half-inferior (e.g., plum, rose, peach).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following is an example of actinomorphic flower?
questions.explanation: Datura is an example of an actinomorphic flower, as it can be divided into two equal radial halves in any radial plane passing through the centre.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Bulliform cells are responsible for

options.b: Providing large spaces for storage of sugars.
options.c: Inward curling of leaves in monocots.
options.d: Protecting the plant from salt stress.

questions.explanation: In monocots, under water-stress conditions, bulliform cells become flaccid, causing the leaves to curl inward to minimise water loss.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In the given figure, which component has thin outer walls and highly thickened inner walls? The figure shows a stomatal complex in cross-section: label A points to the outer epidermal cells, label B points to the subsidiary cells, label C points to the guard cells (the bean/kidney-shaped cells bordering the central pore), and label D points to the stomatal pore itself at the centre.
questions.explanation: In the figure of a stoma with bean-shaped guard cells, A=Epidermal cells, B=Subsidiary cells, C=Guard cells, D=Stomatal pore. The outer walls of the guard cells (away from the stomatal pore) are thin, while the inner walls (towards the pore) are highly thickened. So the answer is C (guard cells).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Parenchyma is living but collenchyma is dead tissue.
Statement II: Gymnosperms lack xylem vessels but presence of xylem vessels is the characteristic of angiosperms.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.explanation: Both parenchyma and collenchyma are living tissues (Statement I is false, since collenchyma is not dead). Gymnosperms lack vessels in their xylem, while in flowering plants (angiosperms), tracheids and vessels are the main water-transporting elements (Statement II is true).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Nucleolus, (B) Centriole, (C) Leucoplasts, (D) Golgi apparatus
List-II: (I) Site of formation of glycolipid, (II) Organization like the cartwheel, (III) Site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis, (IV) For storing nutrients
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Nucleolus - site for active ribosomal RNA synthesis (III). Centriole - organisation like cartwheel (II). Leucoplasts - for storing nutrients (IV). Golgi apparatus - site for formation of glycolipid (I). So A-(III), B-(II), C-(IV), D-(I).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Inhibition of Succinic dehydrogenase enzyme by malonate is a classical example of:
questions.explanation: Malonate resembles the substrate succinate and competes with it for the substrate-binding site of succinic dehydrogenase, so the substrate cannot bind, and enzyme action declines - a classical example of competitive inhibition.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The cofactor of the enzyme carboxypeptidase is
questions.explanation: Metal ions are common cofactors. The cofactor for the enzyme carboxypeptidase is zinc.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Lecithin, a small molecular weight organic compound found in living tissues, is an example of:
questions.explanation: Lecithin (phosphatidyl choline), a small molecular weight organic compound found in living tissues, is an example of a phospholipid.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Spindle fibers attach to kinetochores of chromosomes during
questions.explanation: Spindle fibres attach to the kinetochores of chromosomes during metaphase, when chromosomes align at the spindle equator (metaphase plate).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Chromosomes become gradually visible under light microscope during leptotene stage.
Statement II: The beginning of diplotene stage is recognized by dissolution of synaptonemal complex.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.explanation: During leptotene, chromosomes gradually become visible under the light microscope (Statement I true). The beginning of diplotene is recognised by dissolution of the synaptonemal complex and the tendency of recombined homologous chromosomes to separate except at crossover sites (Statement II true).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are required for the dark reaction of photosynthesis?
A. Light   B. Chlorophyll   C. CO2   D. ATP   E. NADPH
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: For the dark reaction (Calvin cycle), CO2 is required for the carboxylation step, and ATP and NADPH are required for the reduction and regeneration steps. Light and chlorophyll are not directly required in the dark reaction itself. So C, D and E only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: How many molecules of ATP and NADPH are required for every molecule of CO2 fixed in the Calvin cycle?

options.a: 3 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
options.b: 3 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH
options.c: 2 molecules of ATP and 3 molecules of NADPH
options.d: 2 molecules of ATP and 2 molecules of NADPH

questions.explanation: For every CO2 molecule entering the Calvin cycle, 3 molecules of ATP and 2 of NADPH are required (2 ATP and 2 NADPH used in the reduction step; 1 additional ATP used in the regeneration step to reform RuBP).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Formation of interfascicular cambium from fully developed parenchyma cells is an example for
questions.explanation: Living differentiated cells that have lost the capacity to divide can regain it under certain conditions - this is dedifferentiation. Formation of meristems such as interfascicular cambium and cork cambium from fully differentiated parenchyma cells is an example.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Auxin is used by gardeners to prepare weed free lawns. But no damage is caused to grass as auxin

options.a: does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants.
options.b: can help in cell division in grasses, to produce growth.
options.d: promotes abscission of mature leaves only.

questions.explanation: Auxins (e.g. 2,4-D) are widely used as herbicides to kill dicotyledonous weeds; 2,4-D does not affect mature monocotyledonous plants, so lawns of grass are unharmed.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Identify the set of correct statements:
A. The flowers of Vallisneria are colourful and produce nectar.
B. The flowers of waterlily are not pollinated by water.
C. In most of water-pollinated species, the pollen grains are protected from wetting.
D. Pollen grains of some hydrophytes are long and ribbon like.
E. In some hydrophytes, the pollen grains are carried passively inside water.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: A, C, D and E only
options.b: B, C, D and E only
options.d: A, B, C and D only

questions.explanation: Vallisneria flowers are water-pollinated and are not colourful and do not produce nectar (A is false). Waterlily flowers emerge above water level and are insect/wind pollinated, not water pollinated (B is true). In most water-pollinated species pollen is protected from wetting by a mucilaginous covering (C true). Pollen of some hydrophytes (e.g. seagrasses) are long and ribbon-like (D true) and carried passively in water (E true). So B, C, D and E only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.topic: Mendal's Laws of Inheritance And Inheritance of One Gene
questions.question_text: In a plant, black seed color (BB/Bb) is dominant over white seed color (bb). In order to find out the genotype of the black seed plant, with which of the following genotype will you cross it?
questions.explanation: To determine the genotype of the black-seeded plant, a test cross is performed with a homozygous recessive (bb) individual; this cross reveals whether the plant is BB or Bb based on the offspring phenotype ratio.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.topic: Mendal's Laws of Inheritance And Inheritance of One Gene
questions.question_text: A pink flowered Snapdragon plant was crossed with a red flowered Snapdragon plant. What type of phenotype/s is/are expected in the progeny?

options.b: Red, Pink as well as white flowered plants
options.d: Red flowered as well as pink flowered plants

questions.explanation: In incomplete dominance (Snapdragon flower colour), a pink (heterozygous, RW) x red (homozygous, RR) cross gives 50% red flowered and 50% pink flowered progeny.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.topic: Mendal's Laws of Inheritance And Inheritance of One Gene
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Two or more alternative forms of a gene, (B) Cross of F1 progeny with homozygous recessive parent, (C) Cross of F1 progeny with any of the parents, (D) Number of chromosome sets in plant
List-II: (I) Back cross, (II) Ploidy, (III) Allele, (IV) Test cross
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Two or more alternative forms of a gene = Allele (III). Cross of F1 with homozygous recessive parent = Test cross (IV). Cross of F1 with any parent = Back cross (I). Number of chromosome sets = Ploidy (II). So A-(III), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(II).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.topic: Mendal's Laws of Inheritance And Inheritance of One Gene
questions.question_text:
Which one of the following can be explained on the basis of Mendel's Law of Dominance?
A. Out of one pair of factors one is dominant and the other is recessive.
B. Alleles do not show any expression and both the characters appears as such in F2 generation.
C. Factors occur in pairs in normal diploid plants.
D. The discrete unit controlling a particular character is called factor.
E. The expression of only one of the parental characters is found in a monohybrid cross.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.b: A, B, C, D and E
options.d: A, C, D and E only

questions.explanation: Statement B is incorrect (alleles DO show expression in the F2 generation, contrary to what B states). Statements A, C, D and E all correctly relate to Mendel's Law of Dominance. So A, C, D and E only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: A transcription unit in DNA is defined primarily by the three regions in DNA and these are with respect to upstream and down stream end;
questions.explanation: A transcription unit in DNA is defined primarily by three regions: (i) a Promoter, (ii) the Structural gene, (iii) a Terminator.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The lactose present in the growth medium of bacteria is transported to the cell by the action of
questions.explanation: In the absence of a preferred carbon source such as glucose, when lactose is present in the growth medium, it is transported into the bacterial cell through the action of permease.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Clostridium butylicum, (B) Saccharomyces cerevisae, (C) Trichoderma polysporum, (D) Streptococcus sp.
List-II: (I) Ethanol, (II) Streptokinase, (III) Butyric acid, (IV) Cyclosporin-A
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Clostridium butylicum - Butyric acid (III). Saccharomyces cerevisiae - Ethanol (I). Trichoderma polysporum - Cyclosporin-A (IV). Streptococcus sp. - Streptokinase (II). So A-(III), B-(I), C-(IV), D-(II).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Hind II always cuts DNA molecules at a particular point called recognition sequence and it consists of:
questions.explanation: The recognition sequence of the restriction endonuclease Hind II is 6 base pairs long, and it generates blunt ends.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
What is the fate of a piece of DNA carrying a gene of interest which is transferred into an alien organism?
A. The piece of DNA would be able to multiply itself independently in the progeny cells of the organism.
B. It may get integrated into the genome of recipient.
C. It may multiply and be inherited along with the host DNA.
D. The alien piece of DNA is not an integral part of chromosome.
E. It shows ability to replicate.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: When a piece of DNA carrying a gene of interest is transferred into an alien organism, it may get integrated into the genome of the recipient (B) and may multiply and be inherited along with the host DNA (C). So B and C only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell of the plant is called:
questions.explanation: The capacity to generate a whole plant from any cell of the plant is called totipotency.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Bt toxins are insect group specific and coded by a gene cry IAc.
Statement II: Bt toxin exists as inactive protoxin in B. thuringiensis. However, after ingestion by the insect the inactive protoxin gets converted into active form due to acidic pH of the insect gut.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.c: Both Statement I and statement II are true
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.explanation: Bt toxins are insect-group specific, coded by the gene cryIAc (Statement I true). However, the Bt toxin protein exists as an inactive protoxin that is converted to its active form due to the ALKALINE (not acidic) pH of the insect gut, which solubilises the crystals - Statement II as worded (acidic pH) is false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.topic: Population Attributes, Population Growth and Life History Variation
questions.question_text: The equation of Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth is dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K. From this equation, K indicates:
questions.explanation: In the Verhulst-Pearl logistic growth equation dN/dt = rN(K-N)/K: N = population density at time t, r = intrinsic rate of natural increase, K = carrying capacity.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The type of conservation in which the threatened species are taken out from their natural habitat and placed in special setting where they can be protected and given special care is called;
questions.explanation: This describes Ex-situ conservation (threatened species taken out of their natural habitat to a protected special setting, e.g. zoological parks, botanical gardens, wildlife safari parks). Per the printed answer key the labelled correct option is (d).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Tropical regions show greatest level of species richness because
A. Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years, hence more time was available for species diversification.
B. Tropical environments are more seasonal.
C. More solar energy is available in tropics.
D. Constant environments promote niche specialization.
E. Tropical environments are constant and predictable.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.c: A, C, D and E only

questions.explanation: Tropical latitudes have remained relatively undisturbed for millions of years allowing more time for species diversification (A true). Tropical environments are LESS seasonal (more constant/predictable), not more seasonal, so B is false; but they ARE constant and predictable (E true), which promotes niche specialisation (D true). More solar energy is available in the tropics, contributing to higher productivity and diversity (C true). So A, C, D and E only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
These are regarded as major causes of biodiversity loss:
A. Over exploitation
B. Co-extinction
C. Mutation
D. Habitat loss and fragmentation
E. Migration
Choose the correct option:

options.d: A, B, C and D only

questions.explanation: The 'Evil Quartet' - the four major causes of biodiversity loss - are: Habitat loss and fragmentation (D), Over-exploitation (A), Alien species invasions, and Co-extinctions (B). Mutation and migration are not among the major causes. So A, B and D only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: List of endangered species was released by-
questions.explanation: The IUCN Red List (2004) documents the extinction of 784 species (including 338 vertebrates, 359 invertebrates and 87 plants) in the last 500 years.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Read the following statements and choose the set of correct statements. In the members of Phaeophyceae,
A. Asexual reproduction occurs usually by biflagellate zoospores.
B. Sexual reproduction is by oogamous method only.
C. Stored food is in the form of carbohydrates which is either mannitol or laminarin.
D. The major pigments found are chlorophyll a, c and carotenoids and xanthophyll.
E. Vegetative cells have a cellulosic wall, usually covered on the outside by gelatinous coating of algin.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: A, C, D and E only
options.b: A, B, C and E only
options.c: A, B, C and C only
options.d: B, C, D and E only

questions.explanation: In Phaeophyceae, sexual reproduction can be isogamous, anisogamous or oogamous (not oogamous ONLY), so statement B is false. Statements A, C, D and E are all correct. So A, C, D and E only.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Rose, (B) Pea, (C) Cotton, (D) Mango
List-II: (I) Twisted aestivation, (II) Perigynous flower, (III) Drupe, (IV) Marginal placentation
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Rose - Perigynous flower (II). Pea - Marginal placentation (IV). Cotton - Twisted aestivation (I). Mango - Drupe (III). So A-(II), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(III).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I (Types of stamen): (A) Monoadelphous, (B) Diadelphous, (C) Polyadelphous, (D) Epiphyllous
List-II (Example): (I) Citrus, (II) Pea, (III) Lily, (IV) China-rose
Choose the correct answer from the option below:
questions.explanation: Monoadelphous - China-rose (IV). Diadelphous - Pea (II). Polyadelphous - Citrus (I). Epiphyllous - Lily (III). So A-(IV), B-(II), C-(I), D-(III).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: The DNA present in chloroplast is:
questions.explanation: Chloroplast DNA is small, circular and double-stranded, and chloroplasts also contain ribosomes.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) GLUT-4, (B) Insulin, (C) Trypsin, (D) Collagen
List-II: (I) Hormone, (II) Enzyme, (III) Intercellular ground substance, (IV) Enables glucose transport into cells
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: GLUT-4 enables glucose transport into cells (IV). Insulin is a hormone (I). Trypsin is an enzyme (II). Collagen is an intercellular ground substance protein (III). So A-(IV), B-(I), C-(II), D-(III).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Spraying sugarcane crop with which of the following plant growth regulators, increases the length of stem, thus, increasing the yield?
questions.explanation: Sugarcane stores carbohydrate as sugar in its stem. Spraying with gibberellins increases the length of the stem, thereby increasing the yield by as much as 20 tonnes per acre.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In C3 plants, some O2 binds RuBisCO, hence CO2 fixation is decreased.
Statement II: In C4 plants, mesophyll cells shows very little photorespiration while bundle sheath cells do not show photorespiration.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: in C3 plants, some O2 binds RuBisCO, decreasing CO2 fixation. Statement II as worded is inaccurate - in C4 plants photorespiration does not occur at all (not merely 'very little' in mesophyll), so it is judged false.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Identify the step in tricarboxylic acid cycle, which does not involve oxidation of substrate.
questions.explanation: The conversion of Succinyl-CoA to Succinic acid involves cleavage of CoA (substrate-level phosphorylation), not an oxidation step, unlike the other listed conversions.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (A) Citric acid cycle, (B) Glycolysis, (C) Electron transport, (D) Proton gradient
List-II: (I) Cytoplasm, (II) Mitochondrial matrix, (III) Intermembrane space of mitochondria, (IV) Inner mitochondrial membrane
Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
questions.explanation: Citric acid cycle occurs in the mitochondrial matrix (II). Glycolysis occurs in the cytoplasm (I). Electron transport system occurs at the inner mitochondrial membrane (IV). Proton gradient forms in the intermembrane space of mitochondria (III). So A-(II), B-(I), C-(IV), D-(III).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Identify the correct description about the given figure: the figure shows a dense, compact, spike-like inflorescence with numerous long, thin, filamentous stamens projecting outward and upward from it (a grass-type inflorescence with well-exposed anthers/stamens).

options.c: Wind pollinated plant inflorescence showing flowers with well exposed stamens.
options.d: Water pollinated flowers showing stamens with mucilaginous covering.

questions.explanation: The given diagram shows a wind-pollinated plant with a compact inflorescence and well-exposed stamens.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II
List-I: (A) Frederick Griffith, (B) Francois Jacob & Jacque Monod, (C) Har Gobind Khorana, (D) Meselson & Stahl
List-II: (I) Genetic code, (II) Semi-conservative mode of DNA replication, (III) Transformation, (IV) Lac operon
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Frederick Griffith - Transformation (III). Francois Jacob and Jacques Monod - Lac operon (IV). Har Gobind Khorana - Genetic code (I). Meselson and Stahl - Semi-conservative mode of DNA replication (II). So A-(III), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(II).

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following statement is correct regarding the process of replication in E.coli?

options.a: The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in 5' to 3' as well as 3' to 5' direction.
options.b: The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in 5' to 3' direction.
options.c: The DNA dependent DNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in one direction that is 3' to 5'.
options.d: The DNA dependent RNA polymerase catalyses polymerization in one direction, that is 5' to 3'.

questions.explanation: The DNA-dependent DNA polymerase in E. coli catalyses polymerisation only in one direction, 5' to 3'.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: Which of the following are fused in somatic hybridization involving two varieties of plants?
questions.explanation: In somatic hybridisation involving two varieties of plants, protoplasts (cells with cell walls removed) are fused.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text: In an ecosystem if the Net Primary Productivity (NPP) of first trophic level is 100x (kcal/m2/yr), what would be the GPP (Gross Primary Productivity) of the third trophic level of the same ecosystem?
questions.explanation: NPP of 1st trophic level = GPP of 2nd trophic level = 100x. By the 10% law, NPP of 2nd trophic level = 10% of its GPP = 10x. Since GPP of the 3rd trophic level equals the NPP of the 2nd trophic level, it is 10x.

questions.subject: Botany
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Robert May, (B) Alexander von Humboldt, (C) Paul Ehrlich, (D) David Tilman
List-II: (I) Species-Area relationship, (II) Long term ecosystem experiment using out door plots, (III) Global species diversity at about 7 million, (IV) Rivet popper hypothesis
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Robert May - Global species diversity at about 7 million (III). Alexander von Humboldt - Species-Area relationship (I). Paul Ehrlich - Rivet popper hypothesis (IV). David Tilman - Long term ecosystem experiment using outdoor plots (II). So A-(III), B-(I), C-(IV), D-(II).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
A. Annelids are true coelomates
B. Poriferans are pseudocoelomates
C. Aschelminthes are acoelomates
D. Platyhelminthes are pseudocoelomates
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Annelids are true coelomates (A is true). Poriferans to Platyhelminthes are actually acoelomates, not pseudocoelomates (B and D are false as worded). Aschelminthes are pseudocoelomates, not acoelomates (C is false as worded). Only A is correctly stated.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Pleurobrachia, (B) Radula, (C) Stomochord, (D) Air bladder
List-II: (I) Mollusca, (II) Ctenophora, (III) Osteichthyes, (IV) Hemichordata
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Pleurobrachia belongs to phylum Ctenophora (II). Radula (rasping organ) is found in phylum Mollusca (I). Stomochord is found in phylum Hemichordata (IV). Air bladder maintains buoyancy in Osteichthyes (III). So A-(II), B-(I), C-(IV), D-(III).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Pterophyllum, (B) Myxine, (C) Pristis, (D) Exocoetus
List-II: (I) Hag fish, (II) Saw fish, (III) Angel fish, (IV) Flying fish
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Pterophyllum's common name is Angel fish (III). Myxine is also known as hagfish (I). Scientific name of saw fish is Pristis (II). Scientific name of flying fish is Exocoetus (IV). So A-(III), B-(I), C-(II), D-(IV).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Three types of muscles are given as (a), (b) and (c) in the accompanying histology images: (a) shows long, cylindrical, striated, multinucleate fibers typical of skeletal muscle; (b) shows spindle-shaped, tapering, unstriated cells with a single central nucleus each, typical of smooth muscle; (c) shows branched, striated fibers typical of cardiac muscle. Identify the correct matching pair along with their location in human body:

options.a: (a) Skeletal - Biceps; (b) Involuntary - Intestine; (c) Smooth - Heart.
options.b: (a) Involuntary - Nose tip; (b) Skeletal - Bone; (c) Cardiac - Heart.
options.c: (a) Smooth - Toes; (b) Skeletal - Legs; (c) Cardiac - Heart.

questions.explanation: Answer key confirms option (d): (a) Skeletal muscle - Triceps, (b) Smooth muscle - Stomach, (c) Cardiac muscle - Heart.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: In both sexes of cockroach, a pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci are present on :
questions.explanation: A pair of jointed filamentous structures called anal cerci are present on the 10th abdominal segment in both sexes of cockroaches.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Axoneme, (B) Cartwheel pattern, (C) Crista, (D) Satellite
List-II: (I) Centriole, (II) Cilia and flagella, (III) Chromosome, (IV) Mitochondria
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: The core of cilia/flagella is called the axoneme (II). Centrioles have a '9+0' triplet microtubule arrangement in a cartwheel pattern (I). Cristae are folds of the inner mitochondrial membrane (IV). Satellite refers to the chromosome region separated by a secondary constriction (III). So A-(II), B-(I), C-(IV), D-(III).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.topic: Polysaccharides, Nucleic Acids & Types of Bond
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I: (A) Lipase, (B) Nuclease, (C) Protease, (D) Amylase
List-II: (I) Peptide bond, (II) Ester bond, (III) Glycosidic bond, (IV) Phosphodiester bond
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Lipase acts on ester bonds (II). Nuclease acts on phosphodiester bonds (IV). Protease acts on peptide bonds (I). Amylase acts on glycosidic bonds (III). So A-(II), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(III).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Following are the stages of cell division :
A. Gap 2 phase
B. Cytokinesis
C. Synthesis phase
D. Karyokinesis
E. Gap 1 phase
Choose the correct sequence of stages from the options given below :
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is: Gap-1 phase (E) -> Synthesis phase (C) -> Gap-2 phase (A) -> Karyokinesis (D) -> Cytokinesis (B), i.e. E-C-A-D-B.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I (Sub Phases of Prophase I): (A) Diakinesis, (B) Pachytene, (C) Zygotene, (D) Leptotene
List-II (Specific characters): (I) Synaptonemal complex formation, (II) Completion of terminalisation of chiasmata, (III) Chromosomes look like thin threads, (IV) Appearance of recombination nodules
Choose the correct answer from the options given below;
questions.explanation: Diakinesis - Completion of terminalisation of chiasmata (II). Pachytene - Appearance of recombination nodules (IV). Zygotene - Synaptonemal complex formation (I). Leptotene - Chromosomes look like thin threads (III). So A-(II), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(III).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Expiratory capacity, (B) Functional residual capacity, (C) Vital capacity, (D) Inspiratory capacity
List-II: (I) Expiratory reserve volume + Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume, (II) Tidal volume + Expiratory reserve volume, (III) Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume, (IV) Expiratory reserve volume + Residual volume
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Expiratory capacity = Tidal volume + Expiratory reserve volume (II). Functional residual capacity = Expiratory reserve volume + Residual volume (IV). Vital capacity = Tidal volume + Expiratory reserve volume + Inspiratory reserve volume (I). Inspiratory capacity = Tidal volume + Inspiratory reserve volume (III). So A-(II), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(III).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following factors are favourable for the formation of oxyhaemoglobin in alveoli?

options.a: Low pCO2 and High H+ concentration
options.d: High pO2 and Lesser H+ concentration

questions.explanation: Factors favourable for oxyhaemoglobin formation in the alveoli are: High pO2, high pH (i.e. lower H+ concentration), low pCO2, and lower temperature.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Following are the stages of pathway for conduction of an action potential through the heart:
A. AV bundle
B. Purkinje fibres
C. AV node
D. Bundle branches
E. SA node
Choose the correct sequence of pathway from the options given below:
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is: SA node (E) -> AV node (C) -> AV bundle (A) -> Bundle branches (D) -> Purkinje fibres (B), i.e. E-C-A-D-B.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: In the nephron, the descending limb of loop of Henle impermeable to water and permeable to electrolytes.
Statement II: The proximal convoluted tubule is lined by simple columnar brush border epithelium and increases the surface area for reabsorption.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.explanation: Both statements are false. The descending limb of the loop of Henle is actually permeable to water and impermeable to electrolytes (opposite of Statement I). The proximal convoluted tubule is lined by simple cuboidal (not columnar) brush border epithelium (Statement II is also incorrect).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Fibrous joints, (B) Cartilaginous joints, (C) Hinge joints, (D) Ball and socket joints
List-II: (I) Adjacent vertebrae, limited movement, (II) Humerus and Pectoral girdle, rotational movement, (III) Skull, don't allow any movement, (IV) Knee, help in locomotion
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Fibrous joints - seen in flat skull bones, allow no movement (III). Cartilaginous joints - between adjacent vertebrae, allow limited movement (I). Hinge joints - present in the knee, help in locomotion (IV). Ball and socket joints - between humerus and pectoral girdle, allow rotational movement (II). So A-(III), B-(I), C-(IV), D-(II).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.topic: Disorders of Muscular and Skeletal System
questions.question_text:
Which of the following are Autoimmune disorders?
A. Myasthenia gravis
B. Rheumatoid arthritis
C. Gout
D. Muscular dystrophy
E. Systemic Lupus Erythematosus (SLE)
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Myasthenia gravis, Rheumatoid arthritis, and Systemic Lupus Erythematosus are autoimmune disorders. Gout results from uric acid crystal accumulation (not autoimmune). Muscular dystrophy is a genetic disorder, not autoimmune. So A, B & E only.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Pons, (B) Hypothalamus, (C) Medulla, (D) Cerebellum
List-II: (I) Provides additional space for Neurons, regulates posture and balance, (II) Controls respiration and gastric secretions, (III) Connects different regions of the brain, (IV) Neuro secretory cells
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Pons - connects different regions of the brain (III). Hypothalamus - has neurosecretory cells (IV). Medulla - controls respiration and gastric secretions (II). Cerebellum - provides additional space for neurons, regulates posture and balance (I). So A-(III), B-(IV), C-(II), D-(I).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a steroid hormone?
questions.explanation: Glucagon is a peptide hormone secreted by the alpha cells of the Islets of Langerhans in the pancreas. Progesterone, cortisol and testosterone are all steroid hormones.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I : The presence or absence of hymen is not a reliable indicator of virginity.
Statement II : The hymen is torn during the first coitus only.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :

options.a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
options.b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false

questions.explanation: The hymen is often torn during the first coitus, but can also be broken by other causes (a fall, jolt, tampon use, sports activity), and can persist even after coitus in some women. So Statement I is true (hymen presence/absence is not reliable), while Statement II (torn only during first coitus) is false.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a component of Fallopian tube?
questions.explanation: Uterine fundus is a part of the uterus, not the Fallopian tube. Infundibulum, ampulla and isthmus are all parts of the Fallopian tube.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R:
Assertion A: FSH acts upon ovarian follicles in female and Leydig cells in male.
Reason R: Growing ovarian follicles secrete estrogen in female while interstitial cells secrete androgen in male human being.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: A is true but R is false
options.b: A is false but R is true
options.c: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.d: Both A and R are true but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.explanation: FSH actually acts on ovarian follicles in females and Sertoli cells (not Leydig cells) in males, so Assertion A is false. Reason R (growing follicles secrete estrogen; interstitial/Leydig cells secrete androgen) is a true, independent statement.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R :
Assertion A: Breast-feeding during initial period of infant growth is recommended by doctors for bringing a healthy baby.
Reason R : Colostrum contains several antibodies absolutely essential to develop resistance for the new born baby.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :

options.a: A is correct but R is not correct.
options.b: A is not correct but R is correct.
options.c: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A
options.d: Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.

questions.explanation: Breast-feeding during the initial period is recommended for a healthy baby (A true), because colostrum contains antibodies essential for developing resistance in the newborn (R true and correctly explains A).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Non-medicated IUD, (B) Copper releasing IUD, (C) Hormone releasing IUD, (D) Implants
List-II: (I) Multiload 375, (II) Progestogens, (III) Lippes loop, (IV) LNG-20
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Non-medicated IUD - Lippes loop (III). Copper releasing IUD - Multiload 375 (I). Hormone releasing IUD - LNG-20 (IV). Implants - Progestogens (II). So A-(III), B-(I), C-(IV), D-(II).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following is not a natural/traditional contraceptive method?
questions.explanation: Vaults are a barrier method of contraception, not natural/traditional. Lactational amenorrhea, coitus interruptus, and periodic abstinence are natural/traditional contraceptive methods.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Down's syndrome, (B) a-Thalassemia, (C) b-Thalassemia, (D) Klinefelter's syndrome
List-II: (I) 11th chromosome, (II) 'X' chromosome, (III) 21st chromosome, (IV) 16th chromosome
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Down's syndrome - 21st chromosome (III). Alpha-thalassemia - 16th chromosome (IV). Beta-thalassemia - 11th chromosome (I). Klinefelter's syndrome - 'X' chromosome (II). So A-(III), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(II).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one is the correct product of DNA dependent RNA polymerase to the given template? 3'TACATGGCAAATATCCATTCA5'
questions.explanation: Transcription (DNA-dependent RNA polymerase) proceeds 5' to 3' on the RNA product, using the 3' to 5' DNA strand as template. Given template 3'TACATGGCAAATATCCATTCA5', the transcribed RNA is 5'AUGUACCGUUUAUAGGUAAGU3'.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The flippers of the Penguins and Dolphins are the example of the
questions.explanation: Flippers of Penguins and Dolphins are analogous organs, an example of convergent evolution, where different (unrelated) species independently evolved similar traits (flippers) to adapt to a similar environment (swimming in water).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which one of the following factors will not affect the Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium?
questions.explanation: The gene pool remains constant under Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium; this constancy is the equilibrium condition itself, not a disrupting factor. Genetic drift, mutation, gene migration/flow, genetic recombination, and natural selection are the factors that DO affect (disturb) Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are some stages of human evolution. Arrange them in correct sequence. (Past to Recent)
A. Homo habilis
B. Homo sapiens
C. Homo neanderthalensis
D. Homo erectus
Choose the correct sequence of human evolution from the options given below:
questions.explanation: The correct past-to-recent sequence is: Homo habilis (A) -> Homo erectus (D) -> Homo neanderthalensis (C) -> Homo sapiens (B), i.e. A-D-C-B.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Typhoid, (B) Leishmaniasis, (C) Ringworm, (D) Filariasis
List-II: (I) Fungus, (II) Nematode, (III) Protozoa, (IV) Bacteria
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Typhoid is caused by Bacteria (IV). Leishmaniasis is caused by Protozoa (III). Ringworm is caused by Fungus (I). Filariasis is caused by Nematode worms (II). So A-(IV), B-(III), C-(I), D-(II).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Common cold, (B) Haemozoin, (C) Widal test, (D) Allergy
List-II: (I) Plasmodium, (II) Typhoid, (III) Rhinoviruses, (IV) Dust mites
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Common cold is caused by Rhinoviruses (III). Haemozoin is a toxic substance released from ruptured RBCs infected by Plasmodium (I). Widal test is used to diagnose Typhoid (II). Allergy is triggered by allergens like Dust mites (IV). So A-(III), B-(I), C-(II), D-(IV).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Cocaine, (B) Heroin, (C) Morphine, (D) Marijuana
List-II: (I) Effective sedative in surgery, (II) Cannabis sativa, (III) Erythroxylum, (IV) Papaver somniferum
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: Cocaine is obtained from Erythroxylum coca (III). Heroin is derived from Papaver somniferum (IV). Morphine is an effective sedative used in surgery/painkiller (I). Marijuana comes from the flower tops, leaves and resin of Cannabis sativa (II). So A-(III), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(II).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The following diagram showing restriction sites in E. coli cloning vector pBR322: a circular plasmid map labeled pBR322 at its centre, with restriction enzyme sites marked around the circle in order - EcoRI, ClaI, HindIII (upper arc), BamHI and SalI (right arc), PvuII (lower arc), and PstI, PvuI (left arc) - and two gene regions marked as arcs on the lower-left of the circle: gene 'X' (upper of the two, nearer the PstI/PvuI side) and gene 'Y' (below X, nearer PvuII). Find the role of 'X' and 'Y' genes:

options.a: The gene 'X' is for protein involved in replication of Plasmid and 'Y' for resistance to antibiotics.
options.b: Gene 'X' is responsible for recognition sites and 'Y' is responsible for antibiotic resistance.
options.c: The gene 'X' is responsible for resistance to antibiotics and 'Y' for protein involved in the replication of Plasmid.
options.d: The gene 'X' is responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA and 'Y' for protein involved in the replication of Plasmid.

questions.explanation: X = ori (origin of replication), responsible for controlling the copy number of the linked DNA. Y = rop, codes for proteins involved in replication of the plasmid.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: The 'Ti plasmid' of Agrobacterium tumefaciens stands for
questions.explanation: The 'Ti plasmid' of Agrobacterium tumefaciens stands for Tumor inducing plasmid.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Which of the following statements is incorrect?

options.a: Bio-reactors are used to produce small scale bacterial cultures.
options.b: Bio-reactors have an agitator system, an oxygen delivery system and foam control system.
options.c: A bio-reactor provides optimal growth conditions for achieving the desired product.
options.d: Most commonly used bio-reactors are of stirring type.

questions.explanation: Bio-reactors are used to produce LARGE scale bacterial cultures, not small scale, making statement (a) incorrect.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) a-1 antitrypsin, (B) Cry IAb, (C) Cry IAc, (D) Enzyme replacement therapy
List-II: (I) Cotton bollworm, (II) ADA deficiency, (III) Emphysema, (IV) Corn borer
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: alpha-1 antitrypsin protein is used to treat Emphysema (III). CryIAb controls corn borer (IV). CryIAc targets cotton bollworm (I). Enzyme replacement therapy treats ADA deficiency (II). So A-(III), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(II).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
The following are the statements about non-chordates:
A. Pharynx is perforated by gill slits.
B. Notochord is absent.
C. Central nervous system is dorsal.
D. Heart is dorsal if present.
E. Post anal tail is absent.
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: In non-chordates: notochord is absent (B true), heart is dorsal if present (D true), post-anal tail is absent (E true). However, pharynx perforated by gill slits (A) and dorsal CNS (C) are actually chordate characteristics, not non-chordate (so A and C are false as applied to non-chordates). So B, D & E only.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Unicellular glandular epithelium, (B) Compound epithelium, (C) Multicellular glandular epithelium, (D) Endocrine glandular epithelium
List-II: (I) Salivary glands, (II) Pancreas, (III) Goblet cells of alimentary canal, (IV) Moist surface of buccal cavity
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Unicellular glandular epithelium example: Goblet cells of alimentary canal (III). Compound epithelium: found lining moist surfaces such as buccal cavity (IV). Multicellular glandular epithelium example: Salivary glands (I). Endocrine glandular epithelium example: Pancreas, which secretes insulin/glucagon (II). So A-(III), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(II).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II related to digestive system of cockroach.
List-I: (A) The structures used for storing of food, (B) Ring of 6-8 blind tubules at junction of foregut and midgut, (C) Ring of 100-150 yellow coloured thin filaments at junction of midgut and hindgut, (D) The structures used for grinding the food
List-II: (I) Gizzard, (II) Gastric Caeca, (III) Malpighian tubules, (IV) Crop
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Structure for storing food: Crop (IV). Ring of 6-8 blind tubules at foregut-midgut junction (hepatic/gastric caeca): Gastric Caeca (II). Ring of 100-150 filaments at midgut-hindgut junction: Malpighian tubules (III). Structure for grinding food: Gizzard (I). So A-(IV), B-(II), C-(III), D-(I).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Mitochondria and chloroplasts are both double membrane bound organelles.
Statement II: Inner membrane of mitochondria is relatively less permeable, as compared to chloroplast.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.b: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questions.explanation: Both mitochondria and chloroplasts are double-membrane-bound organelles (Statement I true). The inner mitochondrial membrane is relatively less permeable compared to the chloroplast's inner membrane (Statement II true).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Regarding catalytic cycle of an enzyme action select the correct sequential steps :
A. Substrate enzyme complex formation.
B. Free enzyme ready to bind with another substrate.
C. Release of products.
D. Chemical bonds of the substrate broken.
E. Substrate binding to active site.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
questions.explanation: The correct sequence is: Substrate binding to active site (E) -> Substrate-enzyme complex formation (A) -> Chemical bonds of substrate broken (D) -> Release of products (C) -> Free enzyme ready to bind another substrate (B), i.e. E-A-D-C-B.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) P wave, (B) QRS complex, (C) T wave, (D) T-P gap
List-II: (I) Heart muscles are electrically silent, (II) Depolarisation of ventricles, (III) Depolarisation of atria, (IV) Repolarisation of ventricles
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: In an ECG: P-wave represents depolarisation of the atria (III). QRS complex represents depolarisation of the ventricles (II). T-wave represents repolarisation of the ventricles (IV). T-P gap represents the period when heart muscles are electrically silent (I). So A-(III), B-(II), C-(IV), D-(I).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Choose the correct statement given below regarding juxta medullary nephron.

options.a: Loop of Henle of juxta medullary nephron runs deep into medulla.
options.b: Juxta medullary nephrons outnumber the cortical nephrons.
options.c: Juxta medullary nephrons are located in the columns of Bertini.
options.d: Renal corpuscle of juxta medullary nephron lies in the outer portion of the renal medulla.

questions.explanation: In juxtamedullary nephrons, the loop of Henle is very long and runs deep into the medulla. Cortical nephrons actually outnumber juxtamedullary nephrons (making option b false).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: The cerebral hemispheres are connected by nerve tract known as corpus callosum.
Statement II: The brain stem consists of the medulla oblongata, pons and cerebrum.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.b: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questions.explanation: Statement I is correct: the corpus callosum connects the two cerebral hemispheres. Statement II is incorrect: the brain stem consists of the midbrain, pons, and medulla oblongata - the cerebrum is part of the forebrain, not the brain stem.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Exophthalmic goitre, (B) Acromegaly, (C) Cushing's syndrome, (D) Cretinism
List-II: (I) Excess secretion of cortisol, moon face and hyperglycemia, (II) Hypo-secretion of thyroid hormone and stunted growth, (III) Hyper secretion of thyroid hormone and protruding eye balls, (IV) Excessive secretion of growth hormone
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Exophthalmic goitre: hyper-secretion of thyroid hormone and protruding eyeballs (III). Acromegaly: excessive secretion of growth hormone (IV). Cushing's syndrome: excess cortisol, moon face, hyperglycemia (I). Cretinism: hypo-secretion of thyroid hormone, stunted growth (II). So A-(III), B-(IV), C-(I), D-(II).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text: Identify the correct option (A), (B), (C), (D) with respect to spermatogenesis, shown as a branching flow diagram: GnRH branches into two paths - the left path goes LH -> (B) -> Androgens -> Formation of spermatids; the right path goes (A) -> (C) -> Factors -> (D).

options.a: FSH, Sertoli cells, Leydig cells, spermatogenesis.
options.b: ICSH, Leydig cells, Sertoli cells, spermatogenesis.
options.c: FSH, Leydig cells, Sertoli cells, spermiogenesis
options.d: ICSH, Interstitial cells, Leydig cells, spermiogenesis.

questions.explanation: GnRH stimulates the anterior pituitary to secrete LH and FSH. LH acts on Leydig cells to stimulate androgen synthesis/secretion; androgens stimulate spermatogenesis (leading to spermatid formation, labeled A). FSH (labeled the flow's other input) acts on Sertoli cells (C), which secrete factors that help in spermiogenesis (D). So: A=FSH, B=Leydig cells, C=Sertoli cells, D=spermiogenesis, matching option (c).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.topic: Mendal's Laws of Inheritance And Inheritance of One Gene
questions.question_text:
As per ABO blood grouping system, the blood group of father is B+, mother is A+ and child is O+. Their respective genotype can be
A. IBi/IAi/ii
B. IBIB/IAIA/ii
C. IAIB/iIA/IBi
D. IAi/IBi/IAi
E. iIB/iIA/IAIB
Choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: For a child with blood group O (genotype ii), both parents must carry at least one recessive 'i' allele. So the father (blood group B) must be IBi and the mother (blood group A) must be IAi, matching genotype set A (IBi/IAi/ii) only.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) RNA polymerase III, (B) Termination of transcription, (C) Splicing of Exons, (D) TATA box
List-II: (I) snRNPs, (II) Promotor, (III) Rho factor, (IV) SnRNAs, tRNA
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: RNA polymerase III transcribes SnRNAs and tRNA (IV). Termination of transcription (in prokaryotes) involves the Rho factor (III). Splicing of exons is carried out by snRNPs (I). TATA box is part of the promoter (II). So A-(IV), B-(III), C-(I), D-(II).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I: (A) Mesozoic Era, (B) Proterozoic Era, (C) Cenozoic Era, (D) Paleozoic Era
List-II: (I) Lower invertebrates, (II) Fish & Amphibia, (III) Birds & Reptiles, (IV) Mammals
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.explanation: Mesozoic Era - Birds and Reptiles (III). Proterozoic Era - Lower invertebrates (I). Cenozoic Era - Mammals (IV). Paleozoic Era - Fish and Amphibians (II). So A-(III), B-(I), C-(IV), D-(II).

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
Statement I: Bone marrow is the main lymphoid organ where all blood cells including lymphocytes are produced.
Statement II: Both bone marrow and thymus provide micro environments for the development and maturation of T-lymphocytes.
In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect.
options.b: Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct.
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct.
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect.

questions.explanation: Both statements are correct: bone marrow is the primary lymphoid organ where all blood cells (including lymphocytes) are produced, and both bone marrow and the thymus provide micro-environments essential for the development and maturation of T-lymphocytes.

questions.subject: Zoology
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements :
Statement I: Gause's competitive exclusion principle states that two closely related species competing for different resources cannot exists indefinitely.
Statement II: According to Gause's principle during competition, the inferior will be eliminated. This may be true if resources are limiting.
In the light of the above statements, choose correct answer from the options given below:

options.a: Statement I is true but Statement II is false.
options.b: Statement I is false but Statement II is true.
options.c: Both Statement I and Statement II are true.
options.d: Both Statement I and Statement II are false.

questions.explanation: Gause's competitive exclusion principle actually states that two closely related species competing for the SAME (limiting) resources cannot coexist indefinitely, not 'different' resources as Statement I claims (so Statement I is false). Statement II correctly describes that the competitively inferior species will be eliminated when resources are limiting (true).
